full_judgment: 24. It would not, therefore, by very wrong to suppose that the reasons which impelled the authority concerned' not  to arrive at an objective determination of the actual percentage of spirit that is needed for the efficacy of the medicines were actuated by the existence of a wholly different purpose for changing the percentage. This also explains the lack of any serious attempt to obtain the expert opinion. Had it been possible for the authority to claim that Mritasanjibani Sura/ Sudha are not medicinal preparations, nor have they made any stitch claim, there would perhaps be no necessity to obtain such expert opinion, but since these preparations are claimed to be medicinal and which claim has been conceded to by the authority; the inescapable conclusion one must arrive at is that there is the necessity for objectively determining the required Strength of spirit. Such necessity is all the more imperative when it is manifest that the authority themselves fixed the quantity of a certain Tridentate, not quite recently, but since they fixed it, four decades have already elapsed and certainly the correctness of the Presumption arising from the Latin. maxim omniapraes-umanturyesseritaacta, which is also seen to have attached to such act; has not been rebutted by any cogent evidence to the contrary showing that the authority; in fixing the strength in the past, acted wrongly  or did not do it regularly, that is on a proper consideration for  all relevant materials which might have been necessary for determining the strength at "42%".
